clearedSpotChecks.check: Task 2 (L-931): Zora and Soneium have never emitted an ERC-6909 Transfer from the PoolManager, so there are no claims to redeem; every measured redemption on the other networks fits.
clearedSpotChecks.note: I computed the topic with tools/opdiff/evm.py keccak of Transfer(address,address,address,uint256,uint256): 0x1b3d7edb2e9c0b0e7c525b20aaaef0f5940d2ed71663c7d39266ecafac728859, matching src/interfaces/external/IERC6909Claims.sol:14. On https://rpc.zora.energy/ (head 0x33f3f79) eth_getLogs for address 0x0575338e4c17006ae181b47900a84404247ca30f with that topic returned [] over blocks 0x0 to 0x1ffffff, 0x2000000 to 0x2faf07f and 0x2faf080 to 0x33f3f79, which covers the whole chain. A control without topic over 0x33a0000 to head returned 145 logs. Every balance change in src/ERC6909.sol emits Transfer (lines 30, 45, 82, 88), so a holder cannot exist without such a log. I did not repeat the Soneium blockscout query.

clearedSpotChecks.check: Task 3 (L-946): HyperEVM system transactions agree between the official endpoint and nanoreth archives, lead the block, carry 200,000 gas, and none names the PoolManager.
clearedSpotChecks.note: On https://rpc.hyperliquid.xyz/evm I called eth_getSystemTxsByBlockNumber on 20 blocks from 52,246,291 to 52,246,671 in steps of 20. Five held one system transaction each, all with gas 0x30d40 (200,000), none to 0x12D4Fd9C5DeDd00ab8a0bCe2CF0167bbf94b6B1F. For block 52,246,331 eth_getBlockByNumber(full) on rpc.purroofgroup.com lists that system transaction (from 0x6b9e7731..., to 0xb88339cb..., gasPrice 0) at index 0, and the official endpoint returns the same block hash 0x741993bf...1512 with no signed transactions. This fits the ordering that src/PoolManager.sol:279-288 and 349-364 rely on. The research correctly notes that the receipt commitment is an operator-supplied value and not a header proof; my check adds no stronger guarantee.

clearedSpotChecks.check: Full-range swap walks that no endpoint can run in one transaction do not affect user funds, because the loop at src/libraries/Pool.sol:344-348 stops at the caller's sqrtPriceLimitX96 and nobody needs a swap to remove liquidity or redeem claims.
clearedSpotChecks.note: src/libraries/Pool.sol:344 loops while amountSpecifiedRemaining is nonzero and the price has not reached params.sqrtPriceLimitX96, so the caller bounds the walk. src/PoolManager.sol:332-336 (burn) and 291-297 (take) do not touch pool state, and liquidity removal goes through modifyLiquidity, which does not run the swap loop. A long walk costs the swapper gas and does not move others' funds. The answer equality across networks rests on the research's raw files, which I did not re-run.
